title: Inventory movements
description: Full ledger of restocks, write-offs, sales, and other stock changes.

help.title: About Inventory movements
help.overview: This is the stock ledger. Every change to an on-hand quantity writes one row here, and rows are never edited or removed. It answers "why does this warehouse have this many?" — each row shows the change, the quantity before and after, the reason, who did it, and what caused it.

sections.title: What a row records
sections.body: The row is the change, not the current stock. Current stock lives on the inventory row.
items: Product, variant when there is one, warehouse, and the inventory row it belongs to.
Quantity is the signed change: positive in, negative out. Quantity before and after are on hand around that change.
Performed by is the user, and the reference points at what caused it: an order, a shipment, a return request, a stock transfer, a stock count, a till sale, or the inventory row itself.
Supplier, receipt number, receipt files, batch or lot, expiry, and unit cost appear when the action that wrote the row had them.

sections.title: The reasons
sections.body: The reason is set by whatever made the change. You never pick it here.
items: Initial is the opening quantity of a new inventory row. Restock is goods received.
Sale is goods leaving on a shipped order or a till sale.
Return is goods put back by a received return request or a till refund.
Transfer out and transfer in are the two sides of a completed stock transfer.
Adjustment is a stock count or a manual correction. Damage and write-off take goods out without a sale.

sections.title: Valuing stock
sections.body: Inbound rows carry the cost; outbound rows inherit it.
items: A restock records the unit cost, batch, and expiry you enter.
A manual deduction copies the unit cost and expiry of the latest inbound row for the same batch (or the latest inbound row at all), so write-offs are valued.

sections.title: Why you cannot edit it
sections.body: The ledger is the history. Changing a row would make the before and after untrue.
items: Rows cannot be created, edited, or deleted here, by anyone.
To change stock, use Inventory (restock, deduct), a transfer, a count, an order shipment, or a return.
Filter by product, warehouse, reason, or date to audit one item; the inventory row also opens its own history.
